transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Um… I guess I’m here because I haven’t felt quite like myself. It’s not an emergency or anything, and I’m still getting through my responsibilities, but… the part of me that used to naturally reach out to people, or feel excited about work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling, has just gotten very quiet.

I don’t know if that’s the right way to explain it. I’m mostly just moving through obligations lately, and I thought maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been days, weeks, or longer?

It’s been longer than days or weeks… I’d say about eight months, maybe? It started around when we took my older relative into our apartment. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like that’s the only reason, or like I’m not managing, but that’s when I noticed this shift in how I’m thinking, working, and staying connected with people.
Over these past eight months, have you also noticed feeling sad, low, or down in mood most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t think so… not most of the day, nearly every day. I mean, I have off moments, and I can feel kind of flat or discouraged, but I wouldn’t say I’m deeply sad all the time. It’s more like I’m just not as engaged as I used to be, if that makes sense.
Along with feeling less engaged, have you also been experiencing significant worry, nervousness, or tension since this all started?

Um… not especially, I don’t think. I mean, I have normal stress, of course, and I can get a little tense when there’s a lot to handle, but I wouldn’t describe it as significant worry or nervousness. At least not in the way I think you mean. It’s more just… I’m not as plugged in, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you've lost interest or pleasure in almost all of the activities you used to enjoy, nearly every day, over these past eight months?

I guess… yes, in a way. I don’t want to overstate it, because I still do what I need to do, but the part of me that used to naturally reach for people, or feel pleasure in work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling… it’s gotten very quiet. Most days I’m more just moving through obligations than actually wanting or enjoying things. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed a persistent lack of energy or feeling unusually fatigued nearly every day during these past eight months?

I wouldn’t say unusually fatigued, no. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, especially after work or if I’ve had a busy day, but it doesn’t feel like this constant, heavy lack of energy nearly every day. I think it’s more that I’m less motivated or less… pulled toward things, maybe. But actual fatigue, I’m not sure that’s really it.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating, staying focused, or making decisions nearly every day during these past eight months?

I don’t think so, not nearly every day. I mean, I can be a little slower to start things or I’ll put off deciding if it’s not urgent, but I wouldn’t say my concentration is a major problem. At work I can still focus when I need to. I hope that answers it the right way.

I’m not sure I have anything specific to add there. I haven’t really noticed that as a clear problem. I mean, some days are better than others, but nothing that stands out to me as, you know, nearly every day or something I’d want to make sound more serious than it is. Does that answer what you were asking?

Of all the changes you've described, would you say that a feeling of sadness or low mood is the main or most prominent emotional change you've noticed, more than any other feeling like irritability or numbness?

I don’t think sadness is the main thing, exactly. I mean, I do feel low sometimes, but what finally made me come in was more that the part of me that used to reach for people, or enjoy my work, yoga, galleries, even journaling… it’s just gone very quiet.

I’m still doing obligations, mostly. I’m functioning, I think. But it feels more like moving through things than really wanting or enjoying them. I don’t know if that’s the kind of answer you’re looking for.

Has this change in how you're feeling caused noticeable problems in your work performance, relationships, or daily responsibilities—things other people have commented on or that you've struggled to keep up with?

A little, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, because I am still showing up to work and getting through the day, mostly. But… I’ve missed a couple of grant deadlines, which isn’t really like me.

And my supervisor hasn’t made a big issue of it, but she has quietly shifted some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. I think that’s probably because I’m not functioning at my usual level, even if no one is saying it that bluntly. My daily responsibilities are still happening, but not as well as they should be. Does that make sense?
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual—nearly every day?

I don’t think so, no. My sleep isn’t perfect every night, but I haven’t noticed a major change like not being able to sleep or sleeping all the time nearly every day.

It’s probably about the same as usual, I think. I can pay closer attention if that would be helpful.
